name: collapse-recovery
description: Chapter 7: Drive an employee's need gauges to genuine collapse purely through unrelieved neglect. #680's rest fix (resting drains at 0, not idle rate) closed the pathway this file used to rely on: a fully idle employee, even with zero reachable living_quarters anywhere on the map, is auto-routed by autoInsertNeedTasks into a self-targeted, zero-distance ground-rest the SAME tick their gauge first dips under its warning threshold, which now holds flat (0 drain) for the rest's whole duration and tops back up — direct probing (GameLoop.ts, tickNeedGauges/autoInsertNeedTasks) confirmed a purely-idle employee stabilizes in a permanent warning-threshold oscillation and cannot reach the collapse floor at any tick budget tested, with or without a living_quarters on the map. Genuine neglect that still bites (per #680's own acceptance framing, 'a site that genuinely neglects its crew still revolts — the mechanism keeps its teeth', its individual-collapse equivalent) instead requires the employee kept continuously BUSY with no living_quarters ever built: while activeActionId is set, autoInsertNeedTasks only queues a rest unclaimed (never self-claims a busy employee), so drain proceeds at the faster 'working' rate uninterrupted by any rest until tickCollapse's own unconditional threshold check fires — confirmed for real via a direct probe (`employee dispatch <id> x:<own x> z:<own z>` twice, matching the pattern #680's own needs.integration.test.ts CONTRAST acceptance case uses to prove the punishing mechanism survives the fix) and re-derived from that run below, not assumed from the file's old, now-false claim.

expect.note: baseline before the forced-work run below — fresh hire's needs start full. No living_quarters is ever built in this file (deliberate, real neglect) — this driller (seed 42, dusty_hollow, spawns at (82,34)) has no rest destination anywhere on the map.

steps.description: Left unmarked with role bootstrap like needs-collapse-visual's equivalent dispatch: no console command a player would reach for creates a targeted work order at an employee's own position — this exists purely to keep the driller genuinely, continuously busy (working-rate drain, no idle window autoInsertNeedTasks could route a self-rest into) so neglect is real instead of accidental.

expect.note: 25 ticks of continuous forced work (working-rate drain) is not yet enough to collapse a fresh hire — real, verified via a direct engine probe

steps.description: Second dispatch keeps the driller continuously working across the first task's completion, the same handoff needs-collapse-visual's own second Walt dispatch documents — a redispatch issued while still busy is harmless (queues behind the active task) and this one lands right around the first task's own completion, so no idle tick opens up for autoInsertNeedTasks to route a saving rest into before the gauge crosses its collapse floor.

expect.note: cumulative tick 50: genuine collapse via continuous unrelieved forced work, no living_quarters anywhere on the map — re-derived from a real run, not assumed. wellBeing is NOT asserted decreased here: the same batch that drives the collapse also runs the collapse-rest that immediately follows it (no building involved, so it tops gauges back up per NEED_REST_NO_BUILDING_CAP), and a real run shows wellBeing net INCREASE across this step (58.15 → 62.37) even though the employee is flagged COLLAPSING at the end of it — the gauge recovery outweighs the morale hit within this one batch.

steps.description: The collapse-rest above completes on its own (NEED_REST_DURATIONS.fatigue × NEED_REST_NO_BUILDING_DURATION_MULTIPLIER, no building involved) and frees the driller back to idle with nothing queued to claim — this redispatch, and the one after the next tick batch, put them straight back to genuinely neglected continuous work instead of leaving them to recover into the same permanent idle oscillation the file's own description found unbreakable.

steps.note: cumulative tick 75 — recovers from the first collapse, back to genuinely neglected forced work; no assertion here, this batch's own job is only to set up the second collapse checked below

steps.description: See the dispatch two steps above — same handoff reasoning, second redispatch to keep the run genuinely neglectful through to the second collapse checkpoint below.

expect.note: cumulative tick 100: neglect is not a one-off — sustained forced work with no rest destination collapses this employee again. Real run: fatigue back down near the collapse floor, restTicksRemaining active, matching a fresh collapse rather than the first one's tail
